requirements.text: The RLCS Application will provide data to other external systems via an external server data store accessible by other external systems such as ATMS-2, ValuePricing/FasTrak, and ATIS.
The RLCS Application will also allow for remote access through a firewall via outside telecommunications networks by authorized users.
The RLCS software shall send to and receive data from the field device I/O cards through I/O driver software.
All external systems shall retrieve RLCS status from a server outside the RLCS network.

The RLCS shall have a Graphical User Interface (GUI) that allows the operator to view system status, issue commands to change device status, configure the system, export log data, and generate reports.
The RLCS shall monitor all field device sensors, and shall process operator requests for changing field device status.
The RLCS shall execute stored operational control command sequences based on the current system mode of operation and the schedule for each sequence.
The RLCS must be available 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, 365 days per year.
The RLCS shall enforce multi-factor authentication for all remote access sessions and require all remote traffic to be encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher.

The remote dial-in interface shall be replaced with a secure VPN tunnel using AES-256 encryption and multi-factor authentication, or if dial-up is strictly required, it must be protected by a dedicated hardware-based authentication gateway.
The system shall enforce a password policy requiring a minimum of 14 characters, including complexity requirements, and implement account lockout after 5 failed attempts.
The system shall use SHA-256 or a stronger cryptographic hash function for all data integrity and password hashing operations.
The external server data store shall be located in a DMZ, strictly isolated from the internal RLCS control network, and shall only receive one-way data pushes from the internal network.
Define the maximum allowable data loss (RPO) during a system failure, e.g., 'The system shall ensure zero data loss for all transaction logs during a recovery event.'
Specify the maximum allowable latency increase for polling and command execution when the system is expanded to its maximum capacity.
Specify the minimum bit-length or standard for checksums, e.g., 'All control messages shall be protected by a CRC-32 or stronger integrity check to detect transmission errors.'
Define the specific automated detection and switch-over time for each failure scenario (e.g., 'The system shall detect a TMC workstation failure and switch to FCU-based control within 30 seconds').

Define specific latency requirements for GUI screen refreshes and command processing under peak load conditions (e.g., 'The GUI shall update all field device status icons within 500ms of receiving data from the controller').
Specify the maximum allowable increase in system latency (e.g., 'The system shall maintain a 2-second polling interval for all devices even after the addition of two DCU controllers').
Define a maximum resource utilization threshold for reporting tasks (e.g., 'Reporting tasks shall not consume more than 20% of CPU resources or increase database query latency by more than 100ms').

Specify the maximum number of concurrent users the system must support without performance degradation (e.g., 'The system shall support 5 concurrent users with no more than a 10% increase in command response latency').
